sources.role: configuration, input, firmware and state implementation

paths.path: AppleWin.ini beside AppleWin.exe when -conf/-ini selects an INI file; otherwise current releases store settings under HKCU\Software\AppleWin\CurrentVersion (Configuration and Preferences).
evidence: source:AppleWin/AppleWin configuration code and History.txt (-conf custom INI support)

paths.path: AppleWin Configuration > Input writes joystick type, trim, autofire, centering and mouse options to the Configuration settings (INI keys when -conf is used, registry otherwise); keyboard shortcuts are documented in help/keyboard.html.
paths.naming: Source/registry value names include Joystick0 Emu Type v3, Joystick1 Emu Type v3, Joystick Cursor Control, Autofire and Joystick Centering Control; no stable cross-version controller-profile file is documented.

paths.path: Inside attached Apple II disk images (.dsk/.do/.po/.nib/.woz and hard-disk images); AppleWin has no separate game-save directory.
paths.naming: Guest/application-defined files in the selected disk image; AppleWin writes the image according to its disk write setting.
evidence: docs:AppleWin help disk and configuration pages

paths.path: The Advanced configuration Save State Filename defaults to SaveState.yaml in the AppleWin.exe directory; the user can choose another filename/path and F11/F12 save/load the state.
paths.naming: Current state files are YAML save states (default SaveState.yaml); legacy .aws v1 files remain loadable, while newer releases use the YAML format.
evidence: docs:AppleWin help cfg-advanced.html (default directory, SaveState.yaml, F11/F12)
source:AppleWin/AppleWin History.txt (v1 .aws compatibility and YAML state changes)

paths.path: The official Windows distribution includes Apple II firmware under its firmware directory and selects model/card firmware through the Configuration/Advanced dialogs; -rom <file> can explicitly load a custom ROM.
paths.naming: Recognized firmware is model/card-specific (Apple II/II Plus/IIe and Disk II/SmartPort firmware); upstream does not publish a single universal filename/checksum for every image.
evidence: source:AppleWin/AppleWin firmware/ directory and ROM loader
docs:AppleWin History.txt (-rom <file>, Disk II firmware selection)

paths.path: No external decryption/key file is required by AppleWin; the firmware directory contains ROM images, not user key material.
paths.naming: No external key filename or canonical key checksum is published by AppleWin.

linux.reason: The canonical AppleWin repository distributes a Windows desktop executable; Linux ports are separate projects and are not AppleWin's official runtime.
evidence: source:AppleWin/AppleWin README (Apple II emulator for Windows)

linux-flatpak.reason: No official AppleWin Flatpak package is identified; community ports are distinct projects.

macos.reason: The canonical AppleWin project provides Windows binaries only; unofficial ports are not the AppleWin runtime record.
